sections.hypothesis: Buying the calmest liquid coins that break far out of their recent range (a 100-day 3 SD Bollinger breakout, or 20% off the 50-day low) while BTC is in an uptrend, three at a time, and holding until the move reverses beats the large-basket control and BTC at the same exposure on Sharpe, after costs.
sections.rationale: Who pays: time-series momentum (Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen 2012; in crypto Liu and Tsyvinski 2021): traders under-react to a coin's news, so a big range break tends to continue, and trend followers who buy late carry it further. Trading many coins gives trend systems more setups (Rayner Teo's batch 3 lesson). Outside evidence: Critical Trading's tests on S&P 500 and Russell 3000 stocks 2002-2020 (292 and 116 trades, about 50% winners with wins over 3x losses, drawdowns 21-26%; Luke's YouTube batch 2 B1/B2). Honest overlap: Kestrel dropped a channel breakout on BTC/ETH 4h (Sharpe under half of holding) and trend across a 10-coin basket (Sharpe 0.95 vs 1.07 for BTC, and 13.6% of orders under the minimum). This differs in its much bigger breakouts (3 SD over 100 days, or +20%), its calmest-first ranking across the whole liquid universe, and 3 slots of 110 USDT (above the minimum). It is close to dropped strategies: freezing it is Luke's knowing override of the entry bar.
sections.rules: basket-breakout, daily bars, the coin universe (delisted coins included). Eligible coins: 180 days of unbroken history, 30-day median quote volume at least 20M USDT. New entries only while BTC closes above its 200-day average. Rule 1: buy a close above the 100-day band at 3 SD; sell a close below the band at 1 SD under the middle. Rule 2: buy a close more than 20% above the 50-day lowest low; sell a close more than 20% below the 50-day highest high. Both: at most 3 coins at a third each; when more signal than there are free slots, the lowest 63-day volatility first; a stop 3 x ATR(20) under the entry close sells at a close below it (checked at the close: the portfolio engine fills at the next open). Costs from kestrel.toml with each coin's spread band, 330 USDT. Period 2020-01 to 2025-10, before the holdout.
sections.falsification: Against the large-basket control and BTC at the same exposure, with the full scorecard. The idea fails if neither rule passes every test. Few trades is likely (the originals made 116-292 over 18 years across thousands of stocks): under 30 fails test 6, and the spec's shorter lookbacks are not then tried to rescue it.
sections.parameters: rule 1 or 2; band_days 100, entry_sd 3, exit_sd 1 (rule 1); range_days 50 (rule 2); top_n 3; stop_atr 3; trend_days 200; vol_days 63; min_history_days 180; min_volume_musd 20. Two runs: rule 1 and rule 2 at these defaults. The robustness check moves each parameter of each (about 40 neighbours in all); the spec's sweep of shorter lookbacks (20/50-day bands, a 30-day low) is covered by those neighbours, not run as extra settings.
sections.costs: Trades last weeks to months; expect perhaps 10-30 round trips a year across 3 slots, at 22-40 bps each (smaller coins pay wider spreads): about 0.5-1% a year. Trials: 2 runs plus about 40 neighbours.
